subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw replace or augment the current flat `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` run deadline with an idle-timeout plus hard-cap liveness contract, and what config/default shape should own that change?
rationale: The source-reproducible behavior is clear, but the durable fix changes core timeout semantics, resource safety, and likely public configuration defaults, which repository policy treats as maintainer product direction rather than a narrow automated repair.

options.title: Define idle plus hard cap first
options.body: Adopt a maintainer-confirmed contract such as idle timeout for activity gaps plus an absolute max turn cap, then use that as the acceptance target for code, docs, and related PRs.

options.title: Land partial mitigations only
options.body: Review the subagent heartbeat and timeout-notice PRs as separate improvements while leaving this broader timeout semantics issue open.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Close or defer the feature direction and document higher timeout configuration as the supported workaround for long active runs.

recommendation.title: Define idle plus hard cap first
recommendation.body: Adopt a maintainer-confirmed contract such as idle timeout for activity gaps plus an absolute max turn cap, then use that as the acceptance target for code, docs, and related PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current timeout and abort decision surfaces are most recently carried by Vincent Koc's 78399a194cc790bf03c778fe5a67ce594a53bd7d refactor across the central files.
